findings.evidence: Lines 342 and 594 both end in `_of_sum_mul_inner_eq`, while 451 and 504 share `_of_abs_sub_le` and differ only in `setIntegral_…_add` versus `setAverage_…`. Line 594 takes `ha : UniformlyEllipticOn (ball x₀ r) a lam Lam`, and its conclusion contains `|a x i j - ⨍ y in ball x₀ r, a y i j|`.
findings.fix: Name it after the hypothesis that distinguishes it, e.g. `setAverage_ball_norm_iteratedGradient_sub_setAverage_sq_le_of_uniformlyEllipticOn`, and update the references in the docstrings at lines ~79 and ~527.
findings.issue: The PR sets up a pattern where `setAverage_…_le_of_X` is the averaged form of `setIntegral_…_le_add_of_X` (see `…_add_of_abs_sub_le` at line 451 and `…_of_abs_sub_le` at line 504). Under that pattern, `setAverage_ball_norm_iteratedGradient_sub_setAverage_sq_le_of_sum_mul_inner_eq` reads as the averaged form of the constant-coefficient `setIntegral_…_le_add_of_sum_mul_inner_eq` (line 342). It is actually the variable-coefficient estimate with `A = ⨍_{B_r} a`. The suffix leaves out what sets it apart from the `_of_abs_sub_le` sibling: the hypothesis `UniformlyEllipticOn (ball x₀ r) a`.

summary: The theorem that freezes coefficients at their ball average reuses the `_of_sum_mul_inner_eq` suffix of the constant-coefficient estimate, so the setIntegral/setAverage name pairing points readers to the wrong theorem. The other new names (`abs_contraction_le_sum_sum_abs_mul`, `sum_sum_abs_le`, `mul_rpow_inv_mul_mul_rpow_inv`, `addHaar_real_ball_eq_div_pow_mul`, `dotProduct_mulVec_setAverage`, `UniformlyEllipticOn.setAverage`) describe their conclusions and sit in suitable namespaces.
